findings.evidence: Lines 120-125; `Fintype.prod_equiv` in Mathlib takes `[Fintype α] [Fintype β]` as instance arguments precisely so the caller supplies their own.
findings.fix: Take the instance as an argument instead: `[Fintype f.ker] [Fintype {x : G // f x = b}]`, drop both `letI`s, and close with `Fintype.prod_equiv (f.subtypeFiberEquivKer ha) _ _ (by simp)`, which is instance-agnostic.
findings.issue: The statement bakes in `letI : Fintype {x : G // f x = b} := Fintype.ofEquiv f.ker (f.subtypeFiberEquivKer ha).symm`. A caller whose `Fintype` on the fiber came from anywhere else (e.g. `Fintype.ofFinite` after `finite_fiber`, or a `DecidableEq`-derived instance) has a different instance term in `Finset.univ`, so `rw`/`simp` with this lemma will not unify; the lemma leaks its implementation into the public statement.

findings.evidence: Line 120 requires `[CommGroup G]` solely because the product lands in `G`; PR description: "The pullback divisor those go through is the multiplicity-free fibre sum `f*((Q)) = Σ_{fP=Q} (P)`" — a sum in the divisor group, not in `G`.
findings.fix: State it for a general function: `{M : Type*} [CommMonoid M] (g : G → M) : (∏ x : {x : G // f x = b}, g x) = ∏ t : f.ker, g (a * t)`. This subsumes the current form (`g = id`) and weakens `[CommGroup G]` to `[Group G]`, since commutativity is then only needed on `M`.
findings.issue: The product is only over the fiber elements themselves, `∏ x : {x // f x = b}, (x : G)`. The stated consumer is the pullback divisor `f*((Q)) = Σ_{fP=Q} (P)`, which sums the image of each fiber point under the map into the divisor group, not the points of `G`; that use is not an instance of this lemma, so the reindexing API is missing for its own motivation.

findings.evidence: `grep -n fiberEquivKer TauCeti/GroupTheory/Coset/Fiber.lean` matches only `subtypeFiberEquivKer` occurrences and the prose at lines 17, 52, 57; `MonoidHom.ker` is defined in `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Ker.lean:238`.
findings.fix: Say the equivalence is built directly at `MulOneClass H` because Mathlib's `fiberEquivKer` needs `[Group H]`; and drop the now-unused `public import Mathlib.GroupTheory.Coset.Basic` in favour of the `ker` import actually used.
findings.issue: The module docstring states "this one is Mathlib's `fiberEquivKer` composed with the change of presentation", but `subtypeFiberEquivKer` is hand-rolled (`toFun`/`invFun`/`left_inv`/`right_inv`, lines 71-77) and `fiberEquivKer` appears nowhere in the file. The doc misdescribes the definition readers are told to rely on.

summary: The equivalence and its two coe lemmas are a complete, correctly annotated surface, but `prod_fiber_eq_prod_ker` ships an implementation-chosen `Fintype` instance inside its statement and is stated only for the identity function, which the PR's own motivating use (a divisor sum) is not an instance of. The module docstring also misdescribes how the main definition is built.
